forest_start.speaker: narrator
forest_start.text: The orchard road had begun to freeze before Lin Yue reached the pavilion. Leaves rattled in the ditch like shallow bowls. She carried her own bedding, practice pages, cup, sheathed ordinary blade and wrapped pendant; the canal had kept its working equipment and records. No companion had been assigned to follow her. At the gate a boy was sweeping fallen plums into a basket, separating sound fruit from the ones already softened by frost.

forest_01_002.speaker: narrator
forest_01_002.text: The boy offered her a plum before asking whether she wanted a bed. Its skin was split along one side, but the flesh was sweet. Yue ate it standing out of his broom's path. Beneath the pavilion roof, a white branch held three flowers against the cold. Someone had wrapped the tree's pot in straw. The warmth came from a small, tended ordinary brazier rather than any promise that winter had forgotten the orchard.

forest_01_003.speaker: ren_qiao
forest_01_003.text: 'I thought the canal might keep you longer,' Ren Qiao said from the open door. 'Come in before you tell me how it went.' He made room on a bench already crowded with drying towels. Yue had rehearsed a careful account on the road. Sitting beside the familiar medicine cupboard, she found that the first thing she wanted was a bowl of hot water for her hands.

forest_01_004.speaker: lin_yue
forest_01_004.text: 'I have come to check the appointment that was actually kept for me,' she said. 'I would like to hear what happened here before offering another account of elsewhere.' Ren brought the accepted orchard arrangement from its own folder. The page preserved the duties and dates its participants had agreed. Yue set her journey notes beside it, leaving no imaginary visit in the long intervals between the foundry, storm and canal.

forest_01_005.speaker: narrator
forest_01_005.text: Where the paced-breathing arrangement called for her personal return after a month, that visit had gone overdue; the record remained plain about it. Where the accepted arrangement assigned other work, Ren kept those different duties with their owners. Today she was physically here. She could listen to the appointed review, answer for a promise she had actually made, and let the people waiting decide whether another visit would be useful.

forest_01_006.speaker: ren_qiao
forest_01_006.text: 'The people who tried the rhythm remember different things,' Ren said. 'Some remember a little relief. Some remember getting dizzy and being allowed to stop. Nobody remembers your control light as a cure.' Yue looked through the open door toward the treatment hall. The ordinary splints, washing basin and low stools remained. The orchard's work had continued through her absence, acquiring days she could never recover merely by being sorry.

forest_01_007.speaker: narrator
forest_01_007.text: A woman came to collect a bundle of clean cloth and recognized Yue. She asked whether the mountain had sent her to inspect the healers. Yue answered that she had come to hear their review, with no inspection authority over anyone. The woman nodded, asked Ren about a bandage order, and went on with it. Yue felt how easily an old visitor could return wearing importance that nobody had actually lent her.

forest_01_008.speaker: narrator
forest_01_008.text: The matron joined them after her afternoon round. She put three chairs where the sun reached the floor and sat before opening her report. The arrangement's actual review concerned work performed, costs borne and changes made by its own participants. A helper who had refused an extra shift remained in good standing. A patient who disliked a trial still received care. Yue listened to the changes without rescuing her earlier words from their consequences.

forest_01_009.speaker: lin_yue
forest_01_009.text: 'I wanted to return with something that made my absence worth it,' Yue admitted when the report was read. The matron looked at the melting patch on her boot. 'You can return with dry feet and enough attention to listen,' she said. 'Whatever good you did elsewhere belongs to the people there. We have our own work here.' Yue laughed once, surprised by the relief and the sting arriving together.

forest_01_010.speaker: narrator
forest_01_010.text: They agreed on the remaining duties recorded in the accepted page. Any new appointment received a real journey interval and a receiving person; completed work was dated separately from requested work. Ren kept the orchard original. Yue took only the note she was permitted to retain in her personal practice pages. For supper she joined the ordinary table instead of remaining in the report chair, and the matron asked someone else to pour the broth.

forest_01_011.speaker: narrator
forest_01_011.text: The dining room smelled of ginger, wet wool and charcoal. A woman seated near the stove held a child's mitten open over the heat, turning it when the thumb dried. Her coat had a burned patch at the hem. When she saw Yue noticing it, she folded the coat over her knee. Ren introduced her as Shi Lan, warden of the upper forest burns, then fetched another bowl before either visitor could turn the introduction into business.

forest_01_012.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_012.text: 'People usually ask whether I survived the fire,' Shi Lan said. 'I did. The coat did too, mostly.' She rubbed the child's mitten between her palms. 'Ask me whose roof is still waiting for timber if you want a useful question.' Yue set down her spoon. The warden pointed her back to the bowl. 'After supper. You have walked a long way, and I am trying to get this thumb dry before my niece loses it again.'

forest_01_013.speaker: narrator
forest_01_013.text: The niece was asleep on a folded blanket near the doorway, one sock slipping toward the cold boards. Shi Lan pulled it back into place with the practiced irritation of someone who had done the same thing all winter. The girl did not wake. Her guardian's burned coat and steady voice had suggested a solitary person to Yue. The sock revised that impression more quickly than a biographical account could have done.

forest_01_014.speaker: narrator
forest_01_014.text: After the bowls were cleared, Shi Lan laid a forest hiring notice on the table. It offered an eighteen-week commission beginning before the high road froze: fuel measurement, boundary copying, paid safety work and the rebuilding of a winter passage. Qualified wardens retained responsibility for burns. Ordinary meals, lodging, rest turns and return travel were listed against named funds. The village wanted useful apprentices. It had not asked the orchard to send a miracle.

forest_01_015.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_015.text: 'The cutters have two buyers and one wood,' she said. 'Each buyer has a contract that makes sense when you read it alone. Together they ask the same hillside to supply more dry charcoal than we have licensed standing timber for. The buyers say the other man's sacks will be late. The cutters say the cold will be early. I need someone who can keep the figures readable while people are shouting.'

forest_01_016.speaker: lin_yue
forest_01_016.text: 'I can copy and compare a work record,' Yue said. 'I can perform the small prepared controls I have already earned, under their current limits. I cannot carry a fireline or make a hillside grow faster.' Shi Lan studied her face as if looking for the moment that sentence would become a sales pitch. Yue waited. The warden asked whether she had actually walked a fuelbreak in wind. Yue said she had not.

forest_01_017.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_017.text: 'Then you begin with the walking,' Shi Lan said. 'You will learn our signs before anybody puts a command lead in your hand. If you stop because the signs are wrong, put the reason where the foreman has to read it.' She folded the hiring notice without pressing it on Yue. 'Sleep here tonight. I am taking the morning cart north. You can ride beside me if you accept the travel terms.'

forest_01_018.speaker: narrator
forest_01_018.text: The forest commission had sounded, at first, like a sensible next lesson. Then Yue saw the niece asleep under the burned coat and felt the distance between a lesson and a livelihood. She read the meal and return provisions twice. They were ordinary wages for ordinary accepted hours. She could leave at the stated review dates without losing pay for work already done. She asked Ren where the cart road turned after the orchard bridge.

forest_01_019.speaker: ren_qiao
forest_01_019.text: 'Toward the cold hollow,' Ren said. 'The forest has two winters there. One comes down from the weather. The other stays under the burned ridge after the sun returns.' He took the empty bowls to the washing bench. 'People say that poetically. The dead canopy and poor drainage are also practical matters. Shi Lan has been arguing about both for longer than the buyers have been arguing over this year's sacks.'

forest_01_020.speaker: narrator
forest_01_020.text: That night Yue slept in the orchard's spare room with her habitual pack under the bench. The pendant stayed wrapped; its offered memory gave the forest neither timber nor fuel. Through the thin wall she heard Shi Lan telling the niece a story about a fox that stole boots and returned them in the wrong season. The child corrected the fox's intentions. After a pause, the warden accepted the correction and began that part again.

forest_01_021.speaker: narrator
forest_01_021.text: At dawn, Yue paid the agreed lodging charge and accepted the commission's travel offer in writing. The note named Shi Lan's receiving council and the first review date. Ren did not bless her departure as a cure for the orchard's unfinished work. He gave her a route address for actual future correspondence, then stepped aside so the niece could climb into the cart. Yue followed with her own pack and an ordinary cold pair of hands.

forest_01_022.speaker: narrator
forest_01_022.text: The cart left the orchard behind a pair of ordinary draft oxen. Shi Lan sat near the brake, the niece beside her under a patched quilt. Yue took the forward board where she could see the road before the wheels reached it. The driver stopped at the bridge to inspect a plank darkened by last night's ice. Nobody argued that a paid departure time made the plank warmer. They waited while he scattered sand from a box.

forest_01_023.speaker: narrator
forest_01_023.text: On the far bank, small roadside shrines held offerings of split sticks rather than flowers. Shi Lan said travelers left dry kindling for the next person who needed the shelter hearth. The kindling was useful only while someone kept its roof whole. A shrine near the turn had lost three tiles; rain had swollen the little woodpile beneath it. Yue marked the damaged shelter on her personal route sketch and left the wet sticks where they were.

forest_01_024.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_024.text: 'I used to take every broken roof as a message to stop and mend it,' the warden said. 'Then I was late to a burn watch and another person took a double turn.' She moved the quilt away from the brake lever. 'Now I send the receiving village a repair note if I cannot do the job. Sometimes the roof still waits. I have not found an honest method that makes all waiting disappear.'

forest_01_025.speaker: lin_yue
forest_01_025.text: 'How long has your niece travelled with you?' Yue asked. Shi Lan looked toward the sleeping child before answering. 'Since her mother took a winter kitchen post. The kitchen has a sleeping loft for workers, no place for children. We trade weeks when the roads allow it.' There was no heroic rescue in the answer. A useful wage could still require a family to move its tenderness from one house to another.

forest_01_026.speaker: narrator
forest_01_026.text: The road climbed through bare oak. Beneath the trees, young shoots had been cut neatly at the height of a worker's knee. Shi Lan identified the coppice stools and asked Yue to look for the difference between a planned cut and a dead stump. Some stools showed old scars with living shoots around them. Others stood grey and cracked, their roots lifted by frost. A timber tally that counted both alike would promise the next crew wood that could not grow.

forest_01_027.speaker: narrator
forest_01_027.text: At the higher turn, the niece woke and asked whether they would pass the black woods. Shi Lan said they would use the checked road beside them, not the path through the damaged stand. The child pulled the quilt over her chin. Yue looked across the hollow. Burned trunks held the sky in narrow gaps. Snow remained in their shade although the cart road had only frost. Two winters, she thought, and then tried to see the drainage beneath the phrase.

forest_01_028.speaker: narrator
forest_01_028.text: They stopped where a carrier cart had overturned a load of empty charcoal sacks. The driver was already standing, furious with a wheel that had struck the exposed root beside the turn. Shi Lan checked him for injury before asking what he wanted help with. He wanted the axle supported while he fitted a spare peg. Yue held an ordinary timber block steady on checked ground. The niece counted the sacks that had slid toward the ditch.

forest_01_029.speaker: wen_cai
forest_01_029.text: 'Thirty-six,' the carrier said when the child reached thirty-eight. 'Two are folded inside the other one.' He introduced himself as Wen Cai and lifted the folded pair for her to see. 'I do arithmetic badly when I am angry at a wheel. You are welcome to check it.' The child looked satisfied with both the correction and the invitation. Yue liked him before remembering that liking a man told her nothing about his contract.

forest_01_030.speaker: narrator
forest_01_030.text: Wen Cai had brought the empty sacks uphill to the cutters' shed. Their buyer supplied containers, then charged for missing ones at the season's end. A sack caught on the exposed root had torn along its seam. He folded it separately, keeping the damage visible for the receiver. Shi Lan asked whether he had been given the buyer's return conditions. He showed a short printed notice tied inside the foremost bundle, where wet charcoal could not smear it.

forest_01_031.speaker: wen_cai
forest_01_031.text: 'Rong Sui prints the terms,' he said. 'Long Qian has a clerk explain them. My uncle trusts the clerk more because the man remembers his name. I prefer the paper when we disagree about a sack.' He shrugged. 'Sometimes the clerk is right and the paper needs correction. Then I prefer the clerk again.' Yue laughed while holding the block. The wheel settled into its repaired position with a modest wooden knock.

forest_01_032.speaker: narrator
forest_01_032.text: They helped Wen Cai recover the load and left the damaged root approach marked for the road crew. He offered to walk alongside the north cart until the next fork. His own cart could continue at its ordinary checked pace. The offer was companionship on one stretch, not a new commission assignment. Yue moved her pack to make room for the torn sack that he wanted to keep away from the wheel grease.

forest_01_033.speaker: narrator
forest_01_033.text: Wen Cai talked about his sister's marriage feast, for which he had been saving a little from each charcoal turn. The marriage was delayed because the intended household's roof leaked. Neither couple wanted to begin by borrowing more timber than they could pay for. Yue asked whether he minded the delay. He answered that he minded being asked to call it prudent when his sister mostly wanted a dry bed and a date she could tell her friends.

forest_01_034.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_034.text: 'The roof timber is not licensed charcoal wood,' Shi Lan said. Wen Cai nodded without turning to her. 'I know. I have not cut it.' There was enough old conversation in those short answers to make Yue leave the subject alone. A few moments later the warden asked whether the sister had received the council's carpenter quote. Wen Cai said she had and did not know how to accept its repayment terms.

forest_01_035.speaker: narrator
forest_01_035.text: At the fork, the carrier turned toward the cutters' shed and the hired cart descended to the village. Smoke rose from a line of banked kilns on the far ridge. Some stacks sent a thin pale stream into the still air; one plume was thicker, leaning toward the roof of a timber store. Shi Lan watched it through two turns of the wheel, then asked the driver to stop while she sent a warning runner to the kiln keeper.

forest_01_036.speaker: narrator
forest_01_036.text: The runner returned with a message that the keeper was reducing the intake. The thick plume narrowed. Shi Lan did not climb the ridge merely to demonstrate she had been right. The cart carried its accepted passengers on to the receiving village. Yue wondered how many useful interventions ended with nothing anyone wanted to celebrate. Beside her, the niece was counting the sheep in a field, missing one each time the cart's side rail crossed it.

forest_01_037.speaker: narrator
forest_01_037.text: The village's first gate was made of two upright logs and a crosspiece carrying the old boundary number. A pale rectangular patch showed where a newer board had been removed. At the gatehouse an older woman was heating ink beside a covered brazier. She asked Shi Lan whether the orchard healer would come before the next frost. The warden gave Ren's actual offered visit window. The woman wrote the window instead of turning it into a fixed promise.

forest_01_038.speaker: pei_yun
forest_01_038.text: 'I am Pei Yun,' the woman told Yue. 'Stonekeeper until the stones grew legs. Then apparently keeper of arguments.' She tapped the pale patch on the gate. 'That board told visitors the upper wood was closed to common cutting. It cited a boundary marker nobody could find. We took it down after the council asked for the marker. The argument stayed. Give me your commission receiving note before I mistake you for another buyer's inspector.'

forest_01_039.speaker: narrator
forest_01_039.text: Pei Yun read the note, checked Shi Lan's receiving authority, and entered Yue's accepted start date in the work book. She asked which name Yue wanted on the wage record and copied it as given. No borrowed face or old household story was needed at this gate. Yue felt the ease of the ordinary transaction without giving it a speech. She took the receipt and asked where the apprentices ate after the afternoon shift.

forest_01_040.speaker: pei_yun
forest_01_040.text: 'Same place as the cutters when their foreman remembers to release them,' Pei Yun said. 'I keep a cold bowl for the others. They tell me I am too sharp about that. A man who has carried logs all day can survive my sharpness better than another hour without supper.' She pointed toward a low hall beside the council porch. 'Ask for the bread first. They always say the stew needs another moment.'

forest_01_041.speaker: narrator
forest_01_041.text: The bread was hot in the middle and harder at the edge, excellent for dragging through bean stew. Shi Lan took the niece to the lodging room while Yue sat at the nearest open place. A man in a dark fur collar was arguing softly with the cook about how much charcoal the stove consumed. She invited him to prepare supper without it if he wanted a better figure. He stopped arguing and paid for his bowl.

forest_01_042.speaker: long_qian
forest_01_042.text: 'Long Qian, winter-grain buyer,' the man said when he caught Yue looking. 'I measure things for a living and forget when people are tired of being measured.' He pushed a dish of pickled greens toward her. 'Eat. You may decide I am unbearable tomorrow. There will be enough time.' Yue took some greens. He watched the cook add a stick to the stove, then looked deliberately at his own supper instead.

forest_01_043.speaker: narrator
forest_01_043.text: Long Qian's account book lay closed beneath his elbow throughout supper. He asked Yue whether the canal road could carry a winter grain wagon. She described only the checked route she had actually used and the receiving office for current road conditions. He seemed disappointed by the narrow answer. Then he smiled at his own question. 'I did promise you could decide about me tomorrow,' he said. 'Apparently I wanted to start sooner.'

forest_01_044.speaker: narrator
forest_01_044.text: At the end of the table, two cutters compared the weights written on their latest sacks. One thought the buyer's scales were wrong; the other thought rain had made his charcoal heavier than he wanted to admit. Long Qian listened without intervening. Yue had expected a buyer to defend every instrument bearing his mark. He asked the cook where she kept the ordinary check weight. The cook pointed to a cupboard she did not allow him to open himself.

forest_01_045.speaker: long_qian
forest_01_045.text: 'The cupboard has a lock because my clerk borrows things and forgets,' Long Qian said. 'My seal does not make him remember.' The cook brought out the weight and let the cutters test the kitchen scale. It balanced. That told them about the kitchen scale, not the one at the charcoal yard. Long Qian proposed a morning comparison there. One cutter accepted; the other said he would watch before deciding whether to sign anything.

forest_01_046.speaker: narrator
forest_01_046.text: Shi Lan returned with the niece's sleeping roll tucked under one arm. The child had found a splinter in the lodging bench and wanted everyone informed. Long Qian took the complaint as seriously as he had taken the sack dispute. He asked the cook for a small plane and waited while Shi Lan inspected the bench. His concern was ordinary and useful. Yue kept it beside the harder possibilities in her first impression of him.

forest_01_047.speaker: narrator
forest_01_047.text: The apprentice lodging had four low beds and a shelf for dry boots. Yue's bed stood furthest from the stove, but she could close its draft flap herself. She unpacked the cup and inspected the old shoulder seam on her coat. The daily work she had accepted would begin in the morning. She put her practice pages away rather than use a travelling chill as an excuse to repeat tests until one felt impressive.

forest_01_048.speaker: narrator
forest_01_048.text: In the courtyard, somebody was chopping kindling after dark. The blows came unevenly, followed by a curse each time the knot refused to split. Yue found Wen Cai working beside a shaded lamp, his recovered sacks stacked under an eave. He had arrived to deliver the torn one and stayed because his lodging stove needed wood. She offered to hold a light from outside the axe's sweep. He accepted and immediately struck the knot correctly.

forest_01_049.speaker: wen_cai
forest_01_049.text: 'You may be good luck,' he said. Yue moved the lamp a little. 'Or the shadow stopped hiding your line.' He looked at the stump, disappointed to have lost a pleasant explanation. 'The shadow has done much worse things than that. Let me keep this one.' She let him keep the joke. He put the axe down before they began talking, and the workbench became a place where both could stand without watching a blade.

forest_01_050.speaker: narrator
forest_01_050.text: Wen Cai's crew had promised Rong Sui seventy charcoal bags before the first long freeze. Long Qian's agent had also asked them for a share of a larger winter order. The crew foreman believed they could do both if the northern cut went ahead. Wen Cai did not know whether the northern cut was licensed. He knew the men had already borrowed flour against their expected wages. Yue asked what the flour lender's paper actually said.

forest_01_051.speaker: wen_cai
forest_01_051.text: 'If we fail, the foreman pays first,' he answered. 'After that, the paper says the crew's share follows. My uncle signed it for the household because he reads faster than I do.' He picked up the split kindling. 'I read it now. Speed does not help you discover a term that nobody showed you.' He did not ask Yue to declare the debt void. He asked where the commission's contract comparisons would be heard.

forest_01_052.speaker: narrator
forest_01_052.text: Yue gave him the council receiving room named on her hiring note. It was the place for an offered comparison, not a promise that the council could cancel his private debt by lunchtime. He took the address anyway. She helped him carry the kindling inside, keeping each arm's ordinary load modest after the road. When they parted, he thanked her for the light. Neither of them pretended that the light had changed the sack deadline.

forest_01_053.speaker: narrator
forest_01_053.text: Near the gatehouse, a bell rang twice and stopped. Pei Yun crossed the yard with a lantern and an annoyed face. The sound announced a late cart, she said, not an alarm. The cart's driver had come to file a delivery before his order date changed at midnight. Yue returned to her bed while the keeper checked the actual arrival time. Outside her window, the late driver's oxen chewed hay with admirable indifference to midnight.

forest_01_054.speaker: narrator
forest_01_054.text: In the morning, Rong Sui arrived wearing a plain brown coat with good stitching. His boots had been cleaned, but his left cuff carried charcoal dust. He waited until the receiving clerk finished a woman's food claim before setting his own ledger on the desk. Shi Lan called him patient when there were witnesses. He bowed to her with a smile too practised to be warm. Yue saw that their argument had begun well before her arrival.

forest_01_055.speaker: rong_sui
forest_01_055.text: 'The warden thinks a buyer's patience is another instrument of pressure,' Rong Sui said. 'Sometimes it is only the patience required to get a clerk to stop copying last month's figures.' He opened the ledger at a marked page. 'My east-town households need fuel. Your forest needs their payment. If we quarrel until the road freezes, neither party gets what it came for. I am prepared to discuss the actual terms today.'

forest_01_056.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_056.text: 'Then begin with the northern cut your subcontract offered Wen Cai's foreman,' Shi Lan said. Rong's smile faded by one degree. 'A proposed extension,' he replied. 'Subject to the boundary review.' She pointed to the advance issued beside it. 'The flour was delivered without that condition printed on its receipt.' He turned the page and looked at the receipt number. Yue stopped herself from enjoying how quickly a pleasant voice could become inconvenient.

forest_01_057.speaker: narrator
forest_01_057.text: Rong Sui asked for the original flour receipt before accepting the copy as evidence of its terms. Wen Cai brought it from his crew's dry chest under the foreman's permission. The receiving clerk read the words aloud while Rong compared the serial against his own issue book. The receipt charged the advance against northern charcoal but omitted the boundary condition. Rong admitted that discrepancy. He disputed who had removed the condition and requested the subcontractor's retained copy.

forest_01_058.speaker: rong_sui
forest_01_058.text: 'I will suspend collection against that disputed northern quantity while we compare the copies,' he said. 'The crew still owes its confirmed eastern delivery. Do not let my concession become a story that no sack is due.' Wen Cai asked him to write both sentences on the receiving note. Rong did, slowly enough that everyone could read the distinction before signing. Shi Lan accepted the suspension and remained dissatisfied with what it had taken to obtain.

forest_01_059.speaker: narrator
forest_01_059.text: Long Qian's clerk arrived carrying the yard scale on a padded board. The kitchen check weight had been reserved for the comparison, with the cook beside it as custodian. The clerk expected Rong Sui to protest being tested on his rival's morning. Rong instead offered his own known yard weight. Both instruments would be compared on the same level bench. Yue drew separate columns for each result and the condition under which it was measured.

forest_01_060.speaker: narrator
forest_01_060.text: The first comparison found Long Qian's scale sound but its empty-sack deduction too small for the heavier containers used that week. Rong's scale read a little high at the upper range. Neither result alone established intent. The buyers corrected the relevant current readings and retained the first ones in the disputed-payment sheet. A cutter watching from the door asked whether every error could be called accidental. Pei Yun said an explanation would need to face the pattern of errors next.

forest_01_061.speaker: pei_yun
forest_01_061.text: 'We begin by making the next sack's figure right,' the stonekeeper said. 'Then we ask who received too little on the earlier sacks and which records can answer it. Calling a scale sound today cannot absolve yesterday's entry.' She gave the cutter a claim form with room for his own dates. 'This form does not require you to write a motive. Bring what you saw and what you were paid. We can argue about the rest without borrowing your certainty.'

forest_01_062.speaker: narrator
forest_01_062.text: Before noon, the two buyers were seated on opposite sides of the council table. Between them lay two corrected instrument notes, one suspended northern advance and the seasonal cutting licence. Yue's task was to copy the licence's allowed stand into a working map, under the stonekeeper's review. She had expected the work to begin with rows of trees. It began with a line whose omission had already bought people flour they could not easily repay.

forest_01_063.speaker: narrator
forest_01_063.text: Through the receiving room's open door, Shi Lan's niece appeared wearing the mitten that had dried at the orchard. She carried a piece of bread for her guardian and stared openly at the buyers. Shi Lan accepted the bread, broke it in half, and told her where the school meal would be served. The child went reluctantly. Rong Sui watched her departure. For the first time that morning, his careful expression looked tired rather than controlled.

forest_01_064.speaker: narrator
forest_01_064.text: The seasonal licence capped commercial output from the approved stand at three hundred sixty dry twelve-kilogram bags, with household firewood reserved separately. The buyers' confirmed orders and proposed extensions together sought four hundred eighty. The additional northern quantity had no cutting permission yet. Long Qian said his own order could be reduced only if grain-house clients accepted another fuel. Rong Sui said his customers had already paid deposits. The forest did not become larger while either explanation was spoken.

forest_01_065.speaker: long_qian
forest_01_065.text: 'I am heating grain-house kitchens as well as houses,' Long Qian said. 'A cooking failure becomes a food failure before anyone calls it a timber dispute.' Shi Lan nodded. 'And the households using raw firewood are also cooking. You cannot enter their reserved sticks in your charcoal tally because your customers have a warehouse sign.' He ran a hand down the ledger's margin and asked her which alternate suppliers had actually replied.

forest_01_066.speaker: narrator
forest_01_066.text: Only one outside supplier had offered a current quotation, for a limited quantity after its own protected household turns. The quote required carriage over a road not yet checked for winter loads. It might support an order once the route and terms were accepted. It could not fill the present gap merely by lying beside a local contract. Yue copied the quote under proposed supply, leaving the confirmed local cap in its own column.

forest_01_067.speaker: rong_sui
forest_01_067.text: 'If we treat every road as closed until inspected, we will buy nothing before the snow,' Rong Sui said. Pei Yun raised her head. 'The road is not closed by being described honestly. The order is unconfirmed.' He looked at her as though the difference were a luxury. She looked back with the patient anger of somebody who had watched a luxury become a broken wheel. Yue put the road's receiving office beside the quotation.

forest_01_068.speaker: narrator
forest_01_068.text: The council authorized the commission to compare contracts, inspect the licensed stand and survey the contested northern boundary. It did not issue the disputed cutting permission. Shi Lan accepted responsibility for qualified burn planning and ordinary fireline crews. The first fortnight's wages, food and lodging were funded, with a posted renewal review before the next period. The commission's eighteen-week plan could proceed only through those funded intervals, not by borrowing unpaid hours from its hopeful title.

forest_01_069.speaker: narrator
forest_01_069.text: After the meeting, Pei Yun took Yue to the map room behind the gatehouse. Its walls held old sketches rather than triumphant paintings. A table leg rested on a flat stone that had been rejected for marker work. Pei showed the seasonal licence beside a boundary survey thirty-seven years older. The newer document named the old survey but omitted the temporary winter passage drawn through the north stand. The omission did not settle whether the passage still had living users.

forest_01_070.speaker: pei_yun
forest_01_070.text: 'I can tell you people used it when I was young,' she said. 'That is a memory. I can also show you the survey that recorded its permitted turn. That is a document. The present marker should tell us where the turn begins. That is a stone we have not found.' Yue reached for a fresh sheet. Pei placed the old survey within her sight but kept its original edges beneath weighted cloth.

forest_01_071.speaker: narrator
forest_01_071.text: Pei permitted Yue to copy the public boundary and passage clauses. Names in unrelated private settlements stayed covered. The keeper's own childhood memory would accompany the copy as testimony, not secretly change its scale. Yue liked the discipline of the arrangement and disliked how little it settled. When her first copied line leaned toward the wrong ridge, Pei made her start from the marked datum again. A straight stroke could still be a wrong road.

forest_01_072.speaker: narrator
forest_01_072.text: In the afternoon, Shi Lan took Yue along the lower licensed stand. They walked with an ordinary forester who knew the numbered coppice stools and inspected current cuts. The younger shoots were tied with pale cloth; mature marked stems wore darker bands. A few cut stumps lacked either marking. Shi Lan noted their positions without announcing whose axe had done it. Wen Cai's foreman was invited to inspect the findings before the council heard them.

forest_01_073.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_073.text: 'Do not send a practice trace into every tree because you can feel one,' she said when Yue studied a pale band. 'This survey uses ordinary measures. You have not been trained to certify a root's living condition by spiritual perception.' Yue kept her field closed and ran a gloved hand above the band without sampling the bark. The forester showed her the ordinary signs he was licensed to record, then asked her to copy them under his name.

forest_01_074.speaker: narrator
forest_01_074.text: They found a stack of dry billets under a rough lean-to, each cut end bearing the foreman's mark. The stack was licensed household fuel awaiting collection, not surplus industrial timber. A buyer's runner had tied a commercial claim ribbon around its supports. Shi Lan removed the ribbon after recording its placement in an ordinary ink sketch witnessed by the forester. She retained the ribbon as an offered public-work exhibit and sent the runner a receipt instead of a threat.

forest_01_075.speaker: narrator
forest_01_075.text: At the lean-to, an older man arrived pulling a little sledge for his allocated sticks. He had walked an hour on a sore knee. The ribbon had made him afraid that the fuel had been sold away. Shi Lan showed him the household issue list and let the keeper complete the ordinary collection. Yue helped load only the weight he asked for. He left two billets behind for a second trip, refusing to let their stronger arms decide what his knee could take.

forest_01_076.speaker: lin_yue
forest_01_076.text: 'Could a paid carrier take the rest?' Yue asked after he had gone. Shi Lan said the next household delivery review could consider it, with the man's own permission. 'Today he wanted to collect his wood himself. Yesterday he wanted his nephew to help. I will not pretend I know what he wants next week.' Yue copied the delivery question separately from the ribbon claim. One useful proposal did not need to swallow the completed collection.

forest_01_077.speaker: narrator
forest_01_077.text: At the edge of the burned hollow, the air cooled abruptly. Meltwater from the open ridge had pooled in shade and frozen over the low path. The forester used a staff to check the edge while Shi Lan kept both apprentices behind a marked stone. The dead canopy held little snow, but the hollow's poor drainage held ice long after the higher road thawed. Yue could see why a map that showed only elevation had underestimated its winter.

forest_01_078.speaker: narrator
forest_01_078.text: Across the frozen ribbon, a narrow hoofprint led toward a broken stump. The forester compared its size with a remembered track and thought a Frostroot Hart might have crossed recently. He would not identify the individual from one print. Shi Lan marked the sighting location and current path closure. An endangered migration corridor, she said, had once followed the old winter passage. The claim needed current observations and the record that established its protected use.

forest_01_079.speaker: narrator
forest_01_079.text: Something moved behind the stump. Yue first saw a pale antler tine, then a broad head rising above the fallen branches. The Hart looked thin along its shoulders. A dark strand of its rootlike mane dragged behind one leg. It did not approach the people. When the forester's staff tapped the ice, the creature turned sharply, catching a low branch with its antlers and wrenching it loose into the closed path.

forest_01_080.speaker: shi_lan
forest_01_080.text: 'Back to the marked stone,' Shi Lan said. She made the words ordinary and firm. The falling branch struck the place Yue had wanted to inspect. Yue stepped back without reaching for the sheathed blade. A creature that had once accepted orchard pain could still hurt a person standing too near its antlers. Its earlier kindness did not turn the current narrow space into safe ground.

forest_01_081.speaker: narrator
forest_01_081.text: They gave the Hart a clear path into the farther trees. It moved slowly at first, then quicker when the branch released its antlers. The mane strand remained caught near the stump. The forester did not follow to collect it. He could record the visible obstruction from the public path and ask the habitat keeper about later access. Shi Lan watched until the pale head vanished before permitting the crew to return along its checked route.

forest_01_082.speaker: narrator
forest_01_082.text: On the way back, Yue thought of the broad copper rest in the orchard pavilion. She had known the Hart as a tired visitor with the right to decline another exchange. Here she had seen a large frightened body break wood beside a frozen track. Both encounters could be true. She put the dangerous movement in the field report without turning it into a claim that the creature had intended to attack them.

forest_01_083.speaker: narrator
forest_01_083.text: At the village, Wen Cai's foreman inspected the unmarked-stump note and requested another day to compare crew marks. Rong Sui's runner accepted the ribbon receipt without admitting his employer had authorized the claim. Pei Yun put the new track observation beside the old passage survey. Long Qian asked whether any of it changed tomorrow's confirmed eastern delivery. Shi Lan answered that the household stack remained reserved and the northern cut remained unlicensed.

forest_01_084.speaker: narrator
forest_01_084.text: Yue returned to the apprentice room after supper with mud on her coat and no bright discovery to polish. Beneath the ridge, one winter came from contracts that had spent wood before it was permitted. Another lay in a hollow where a living animal could not turn without breaking branches. She hung the coat where it could dry, ate the bread she had saved, and began a clean copy of the day's actual work before sleep.
